title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last sheet (p.131) of the folder. It is the blank back of an IHES letterhead, written upside down and with very little on it. The marks are pencil scribbles that appear to explain the simplest singular curve, the ordinary node.

- **The node.** Two crossing lines are drawn, the curve X: xy = 0 in the plane. Next to them is written x^2 - y^2, which over a field of characteristic not 2 is the same node after the linear change of variables u = x+y, v = x-y, since x^2 - y^2 = uv.
- **Its coordinate ring.** k[x,y]/(xy) is the coordinate ring of the node. Its normalization is k[x] × k[y], i.e. two disjoint lines.
- **The two components.** The note 'P^1, P^1' plausibly refers to the projective version: two P^1's meeting in one point, or the normalization being two disjoint P^1's.
- **Segments with marked points.** Several short segments each carry one marked point. They look like pictures of the two branches separated, each with the preimage of the node marked. Equally they could be lines through a point in various directions, i.e. a pencil, or tangent directions.
- **Other marks.** A partly struck-out 'k[x]' or 'k[X]' (perhaps k[ε] or k[[x]]) and an isolated vertical mark complete the page.

**Link to the previous page.** The previous page proves, via the blow-up X' → X along C and an incidence family over S, that A(Y(y)) = Im A(X) + Im A(C), with a graded version A^i(Y(y)) = Im A^i(X) + Im A^{i-j}(C). That is a Lefschetz-type statement for Chow groups of the members Y(y) of a family. The node sketch may be a note on the degenerate members of such a family, since singular fibres of a Lefschetz pencil have ordinary double points. It may equally be an unrelated explanation scribbled on scrap paper, perhaps for a visitor or student. Nothing on the page develops a mathematical argument.
errors: No assertions are made on the page, so there is nothing to check. Note only that x^2 - y^2 is equivalent to xy (two crossing lines) only when char k ≠ 2.

ideas.what: Ordinary double point (node) xy=0, equivalently x^2-y^2, with its coordinate ring k[x,y]/(xy) and two branches / normalization (two P^1's or two lines with marked points)
ideas.modern_name: Node; normalization of a nodal curve; two-component degeneration
ideas.where_published: Standard material; nodes appear e.g. in SGA 7 (Picard–Lefschetz) and in the stable-curves context

deep.surprise_reason: These are scrap-paper sketches of a node and its coordinate ring on the back of a letterhead. There is no argument or new claim; at most a weak, speculative link to the Lefschetz-pencil computation on the previous page.
transcription_corrections: The sheet is written upside down relative to the IHES letterhead; the handwritten notes run along the left margin when the image is viewed as given.
The first item at bottom left looks like a struck-through 'k[x]' (or 'k[X]'); it is partly crossed out.
'P^1, P^1' is uncertain; it may read 'P^1, P^1' denoting two components, consistent with the two-lines picture.
The faint large pencil letters at top right (resembling 'Z'/'W' with a blue stroke) are probably not mathematics; there is also show-through from the reverse side.
